title: Why Do We Keep Checking the Fridge?

scenes.caption: WHY DO WE KEEP CHECKING THE FRIDGE?
scenes.narration: You already checked the fridge. Nothing changed. So why are you opening it again five minutes later?

scenes.caption: YOUR BRAIN EXPECTS A REWARD
scenes.narration: Part of the answer is simple. Your brain likes the possibility of a reward, even when the odds are terrible.

scenes.caption: BOREDOM → CHECK → MAYBE FOOD
scenes.narration: When you are bored, stressed, or procrastinating, checking the fridge becomes a tiny habit loop.

scenes.caption: NOT ALWAYS HUNGER
scenes.narration: And sometimes you are not actually hungry. You just want stimulation, comfort, or something to do.

scenes.caption: HUNGER vs HABIT
scenes.narration: Real hunger usually builds gradually. Habit checking can appear suddenly, especially when you walk past the kitchen.

scenes.caption: CUE → ROUTINE → REWARD
scenes.narration: The kitchen is the cue. Opening the fridge is the routine. Finding something tasty is the possible reward.

scenes.caption: YOUR FRIDGE DID NOT UPDATE
scenes.narration: So yes, your brain can treat the fridge like a social media feed that might somehow have new content.

scenes.caption: YOU WILL STILL CHECK AGAIN
scenes.narration: Now that you know this, you will definitely stop checking the fridge for no reason. Probably. Maybe. Check again later.
